items.q: Fixed spending is 120000 naira a period and variable spending is 32 naira per unit. What is the total cost of 6000 units?
items.s: Total cost = fixed + variable x units = 120000 + 32 x 6000 = 312000 naira.

items.q: An item is used at a maximum of 750 units a week and the longest delivery delay is 4 weeks. What reorder level should be set?
items.s: Reorder level = maximum usage x maximum lead time = 750 x 4 = 3000 units.

items.q: Workers put in 600 hours at 350 naira an hour to make 800 units. What is the labour cost per unit?
items.s: Labour cost per unit = (600 x 350)/800 = 262.5 naira.

items.q: Rent of 480000 naira is shared between three departments in the ratio 4:2:3 by floor area. What amount is charged to the first department?
items.s: Share = total x ratio/total ratio = 480000 x 4/9 = 213333.33 naira.

items.q: Fixed costs are 120000 naira a period. Each unit sells for 125 naira and has a variable cost of 55 naira. What is the break even point in units?
items.s: Break even units = fixed costs/contribution per unit = 120000/(125 - 55) = 1714.29 units.

items.q: Budgeted sales are 9000 units. Opening stock is 1200 units and the firm wants 1500 units left at the end. How many units must be produced?
items.s: Production = sales + closing stock - opening stock = 9000 + 1500 - 1200 = 9300 units.

items.q: A factory produced 2500 units in a period and incurred 240000 naira of material, 290000 naira of labour and 150000 naira of overheads. What is the cost per unit?
A firm uses 25000 units of an item a year. Each order costs 90 naira to place and holding costs 8 naira per unit a year. What is the economic order quantity?
items.s: EOQ = square root of (2 x annual demand x ordering cost / holding cost) = square root of (2 x 25000 x 90 / 8) = 750 units.

items.q: The reorder level of an item is 3000 units and the reorder quantity is 1500 units. Minimum usage is 300 units a week over a minimum lead time of 2 weeks. What is the maximum stock level?
items.s: Maximum level = reorder level + reorder quantity - (minimum usage x minimum lead time) = 3000 + 1500 - 300 x 2 = 3900 units.

items.q: The reorder level of an item is 3000 units. Average usage is 500 units a week and the average lead time is 4 weeks. What is the minimum stock level?
items.s: Minimum level = reorder level - (average usage x average lead time) = 3000 - 500 x 4 = 1000 units.

items.q: The cost of goods sold in a year was 720000 naira. Opening stock was 120000 naira and closing stock was 110000 naira. What is the stock turnover rate?
A store held 100 units at 12 naira each and then received 400 units at 30 naira each. 250 units were issued. Using FIFO, what is the value of the issue?
items.s: FIFO takes the oldest units first: 100 x 12 + 150 x 30 = 5700 naira.

items.q: A store held 200 units at 10 naira each and then received 400 units at 22 naira each. 150 units were issued immediately afterwards. Using LIFO, what is the value of the issue?
items.s: LIFO takes the newest units first: 150 x 22 = 3300 naira.

items.q: A store held 400 units at 20 naira each and received 200 units at 30 naira each. What is the weighted average price per unit?
items.s: Weighted average = (400 x 20 + 200 x 30)/(400 + 200) = 23.33 naira.

items.q: A worker is paid 750 naira an hour for a standard week of 200 hours and one and a half times that for overtime. He worked 20 hours of overtime. What is his gross pay?
items.s: Gross pay = 200 x 750 + 20 x 750 x 1.5 = 172500 naira.

items.q: A worker earning 400 naira an hour worked 12 hours of overtime at time and a half. What is the overtime premium charged to overhead?
items.s: Premium = overtime hours x hourly rate x 0.5 = 12 x 400 x 0.5 = 2400 naira.

items.q: Budgeted overheads for a year are 600000 naira and budgeted labour hours are 30000. What is the overhead absorption rate per labour hour?
items.s: Absorption rate = budgeted overheads/budgeted hours = 600000/30000 = 20 naira per hour.

items.q: Budgeted overheads are 900000 naira for 15000 budgeted hours. Actual hours worked were 21000 and actual overheads were 900000 naira. Taking absorbed minus incurred, what is the over or under absorption figure?
items.s: Absorption rate = 900000/15000 = 60 per hour; absorbed = 60 x 21000 = 1260000; figure = absorbed - incurred = 1260000 - 900000 = 360000 naira, an amount of over absorption.

items.q: A department expects to incur 540000 naira of overheads and to run its machines for 2700 hours. What is the machine hour rate?
items.s: Machine hour rate = overheads/machine hours = 540000/2700 = 200 naira per hour.

items.q: A job used 180000 naira of material, 80000 naira of labour and 60000 naira of overheads. The firm quotes a price with a profit of 30 percent on total cost. What is the price?
Work certified on a contract to date is 1200000 naira and the contract provides for retention of 15 percent. What amount is held back?
items.s: Retention = 1200000 x 15/100 = 180000 naira.

items.q: The value of work certified on an unfinished contract is 1300000 naira and the cost incurred to date is 1000000 naira. What is the notional profit?
items.s: Notional profit = value certified - cost to date = 1300000 - 1000000 = 300000 naira.

items.q: A process finished and transferred 4000 units and left 1600 units in progress which are 50 percent complete. What are the equivalent units of production?
items.s: Equivalent units = completed + closing work in progress x degree of completion = 4000 + 1600 x 50/100 = 4800 units.

items.q: A process takes in 10000 units at a total cost of 960000 naira. Normal loss is 5 percent of input and the loss sells for 8 naira a unit. What is the cost per good unit?
items.s: Normal loss = 500 units worth 4000 naira; cost per good unit = (960000 - 4000)/(10000 - 500) = 100.63 naira.

items.q: A process put in 8000 units. Normal loss is 5 percent of input and actual output was 7000 units. What is the number of abnormal loss units?
items.s: Expected output = 8000 - 400 = 7600 units; abnormal loss = 7600 - 7000 = 600 units.

items.q: A product sells for 120 naira a unit and has variable costs of 70 naira a unit. Fixed costs are 90000 naira a period and 1500 units are sold. What is the profit?
items.s: Profit = (selling price - variable cost) x units - fixed costs = (120 - 70) x 1500 - 90000 = -15000 naira.

items.q: Fixed costs are 360000 naira a period and the contribution to sales ratio is 40 percent. What is the break even sales revenue?
items.s: Break even revenue = fixed costs/contribution ratio = 360000/0.4 = 900000 naira.

items.q: A firm sells 8000 units against a break even volume of 5000 units. Each unit sells for 120 naira. What is the margin of safety in naira?
items.s: Margin of safety = (8000 - 5000) x 120 = 360000 naira.

items.q: A product sells for 120 naira a unit and its variable cost is 120 naira a unit. What is the profit volume ratio?
items.s: Profit volume ratio = (selling price - variable cost)/selling price x 100 = (120 - 120)/120 x 100 = 0 percent.

items.q: Fixed costs are 160000 naira and the firm wants a profit of 50000 naira. Each unit contributes 40 naira. How many units must be sold?
items.s: Units = (fixed costs + target profit)/contribution per unit = (160000 + 50000)/40 = 5250 units.

items.q: A cash budget opens with a balance of 80000 naira. Receipts for the month are 360000 naira and payments are 180000 naira. What is the closing balance?
items.s: Closing balance = opening balance + receipts - payments = 80000 + 360000 - 180000 = 260000 naira.

items.q: A firm bought and used 2000 kg of material. The standard price was 12 naira a kg and the actual price was 22 naira a kg. What is the material price variance?
items.s: Price variance = (standard price - actual price) x quantity = (12 - 22) x 2000 = -20000 naira.

items.q: Production was 2000 units. The standard allowance is 5 kg a unit and 5 kg a unit were actually used. Material is valued at 12 naira a kg. What is the material usage variance?
items.s: Usage variance = (standard quantity - actual quantity) x standard price = (10000 - 10000) x 12 = 0 naira.

items.q: Workers worked 1200 hours. The standard rate was 500 naira an hour and the actual rate paid was 540 naira an hour. What is the labour rate variance?
items.s: Rate variance = (standard rate - actual rate) x hours = (500 - 540) x 1200 = -48000 naira.

items.q: A firm made 800 units. The standard time allowed is 4 hours a unit and 5 hours a unit were actually worked. The standard rate is 350 naira an hour. What is the labour efficiency variance?
items.s: Efficiency variance = (standard hours - actual hours) x standard rate = (3200 - 4000) x 350 = -280000 naira.

items.q: A batch uses 48000 naira of material, 30000 naira of direct labour and 12000 naira of direct expenses. What is the prime cost?
items.s: Prime cost = material + direct labour + direct expenses = 48000 + 30000 + 12000 = 90000 naira.

items.q: Fixed spending is 180000 naira a period and variable spending is 45 naira per unit. What is the total cost of 4000 units?
items.s: Total cost = fixed + variable x units = 180000 + 45 x 4000 = 360000 naira.

items.q: An item is used at a maximum of 400 units a week and the longest delivery delay is 4 weeks. What reorder level should be set?

items.q: Workers put in 600 hours at 500 naira an hour to make 400 units. What is the labour cost per unit?
items.s: Labour cost per unit = (600 x 500)/400 = 750 naira.

items.q: Rent of 960000 naira is shared between three departments in the ratio 4:2:2 by floor area. What amount is charged to the first department?
items.s: Share = total x ratio/total ratio = 960000 x 4/8 = 480000 naira.

items.q: Budgeted sales are 6000 units. Opening stock is 500 units and the firm wants 900 units left at the end. How many units must be produced?
items.s: Production = sales + closing stock - opening stock = 6000 + 900 - 500 = 6400 units.

items.q: A factory produced 2000 units in a period and incurred 480000 naira of material, 290000 naira of labour and 120000 naira of overheads. What is the cost per unit?
A firm uses 9000 units of an item a year. Each order costs 50 naira to place and holding costs 8 naira per unit a year. What is the economic order quantity?
items.s: EOQ = square root of (2 x annual demand x ordering cost / holding cost) = square root of (2 x 9000 x 50 / 8) = 335.41 units.

items.q: The reorder level of an item is 2400 units and the reorder quantity is 1500 units. Minimum usage is 200 units a week over a minimum lead time of 3 weeks. What is the maximum stock level?
items.s: Maximum level = reorder level + reorder quantity - (minimum usage x minimum lead time) = 2400 + 1500 - 200 x 3 = 3300 units.

items.q: The reorder level of an item is 5400 units. Average usage is 400 units a week and the average lead time is 4 weeks. What is the minimum stock level?
items.s: Minimum level = reorder level - (average usage x average lead time) = 5400 - 400 x 4 = 3800 units.

items.q: The cost of goods sold in a year was 480000 naira. Opening stock was 90000 naira and closing stock was 80000 naira. What is the stock turnover rate?
A store held 300 units at 12 naira each and then received 300 units at 30 naira each. 350 units were issued. Using FIFO, what is the value of the issue?
items.s: FIFO takes the oldest units first: 300 x 12 + 50 x 30 = 5100 naira.

items.q: A store held 200 units at 18 naira each and then received 300 units at 28 naira each. 250 units were issued immediately afterwards. Using LIFO, what is the value of the issue?
items.s: LIFO takes the newest units first: 250 x 28 = 7000 naira.

items.q: A store held 200 units at 12 naira each and received 200 units at 26 naira each. What is the weighted average price per unit?
items.s: Weighted average = (200 x 12 + 200 x 26)/(200 + 200) = 19 naira.

items.q: A worker is paid 450 naira an hour for a standard week of 160 hours and one and a half times that for overtime. He worked 10 hours of overtime. What is his gross pay?
items.s: Gross pay = 160 x 450 + 10 x 450 x 1.5 = 78750 naira.

items.q: A worker earning 700 naira an hour worked 16 hours of overtime at time and a half. What is the overtime premium charged to overhead?
items.s: Premium = overtime hours x hourly rate x 0.5 = 16 x 700 x 0.5 = 5600 naira.

items.q: Budgeted overheads for a year are 1200000 naira and budgeted labour hours are 30000. What is the overhead absorption rate per labour hour?
items.s: Absorption rate = budgeted overheads/budgeted hours = 1200000/30000 = 40 naira per hour.

items.q: Budgeted overheads are 1200000 naira for 15000 budgeted hours. Actual hours worked were 28000 and actual overheads were 1200000 naira. Taking absorbed minus incurred, what is the over or under absorption figure?
items.s: Absorption rate = 1200000/15000 = 80 per hour; absorbed = 80 x 28000 = 2240000; figure = absorbed - incurred = 2240000 - 1200000 = 1040000 naira, an amount of over absorption.

items.q: A department expects to incur 810000 naira of overheads and to run its machines for 1800 hours. What is the machine hour rate?
items.s: Machine hour rate = overheads/machine hours = 810000/1800 = 450 naira per hour.

items.q: A job used 180000 naira of material, 80000 naira of labour and 90000 naira of overheads. The firm quotes a price with a profit of 30 percent on total cost. What is the price?
Work certified on a contract to date is 1500000 naira and the contract provides for retention of 10 percent. What amount is held back?
items.s: Retention = 1500000 x 10/100 = 150000 naira.

items.q: A process finished and transferred 8000 units and left 1600 units in progress which are 50 percent complete. What are the equivalent units of production?
items.s: Equivalent units = completed + closing work in progress x degree of completion = 8000 + 1600 x 50/100 = 8800 units.

items.q: A process takes in 10000 units at a total cost of 450000 naira. Normal loss is 5 percent of input and the loss sells for 2 naira a unit. What is the cost per good unit?
items.s: Normal loss = 500 units worth 1000 naira; cost per good unit = (450000 - 1000)/(10000 - 500) = 47.26 naira.

items.q: A process put in 8000 units. Normal loss is 10 percent of input and actual output was 3400 units. What is the number of abnormal loss units?
items.s: Expected output = 8000 - 800 = 7200 units; abnormal loss = 7200 - 3400 = 3800 units.

items.q: A product sells for 150 naira a unit and has variable costs of 90 naira a unit. Fixed costs are 60000 naira a period and 1500 units are sold. What is the profit?
items.s: Profit = (selling price - variable cost) x units - fixed costs = (150 - 90) x 1500 - 60000 = 30000 naira.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines net pay?
o: two or more items of significant value produced together from the same input
the method used for large long term works carried out at the site of the customer
the amount a worker actually receives after deductions
a section of the business for which expenditure is gathered and charged separately
items.s: net pay: the amount a worker actually receives after deductions. The other options describe contract costing, cost centre, joint products.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines maximum level.
o: a situation in which an item is needed for production but none is held
a pay system in which the worker receives a fixed amount for each item produced
the highest holding allowed without risking waste or excess storage charges
the extra above the normal hourly amount paid for hours beyond the standard
items.s: maximum level: the highest holding allowed without risking waste or excess storage charges. The other options describe overtime premium, piece rate, stock out.

items.q: Which term is described by “the effect of paying a different hourly amount from the one planned”?
o: labour efficiency variance
labour rate variance
variance
favourable variance
items.s: labour rate variance is the effect of paying a different hourly amount from the one planned.

items.q: budgetary control may be defined as
o: a difference that raises profit compared with the plan
the pricing rule under which the newest consignment is treated as issued first
the total of all spending that cannot be traced to a single item
the practice of comparing actual results with the plan and acting on the differences
items.s: budgetary control: the practice of comparing actual results with the plan and acting on the differences. The other options describe lifo, favourable variance, overhead.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines normal loss.
o: the unavoidable waste expected in a process under ordinary working conditions
the holding at which a fresh order should be placed
the charging of a whole item of spending to the one section that caused it
the recovery of indirect spending into the figure carried by each product using a chosen rate
items.s: normal loss: the unavoidable waste expected in a process under ordinary working conditions. The other options describe allocation, absorption, reorder level.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines idle time?
o: paid hours during which no production takes place because of breakdown or waiting
the holding at which a fresh order should be placed
a section of the business for which expenditure is gathered and charged separately
a forecast of the quantities to be made in each period
items.s: idle time: paid hours during which no production takes place because of breakdown or waiting. The other options describe reorder level, cost centre, production budget.

items.q: Which term is described by “the record kept at the store showing quantities received, issued and on hand”?
o: bin card
maximum level
minimum level
stores ledger
items.s: bin card is the record kept at the store showing quantities received, issued and on hand.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines blanket rate.
o: a rate obtained by dividing the total value of goods available by the total quantity
the pricing rule under which the oldest consignment is treated as issued first
a single recovery figure applied to the whole factory instead of separate departmental ones
the effect of working faster or slower than the hours allowed
items.s: blanket rate: a single recovery figure applied to the whole factory instead of separate departmental ones. The other options describe weighted average price, labour efficiency variance, fifo.

items.q: Which term is described by “the expression of partly finished work in terms of fully finished items”?
o: split off point
equivalent units
normal loss account
process account
items.s: equivalent units is the expression of partly finished work in terms of fully finished items.

items.q: The statement “a difference that raises profit compared with the plan” describes which of the following?
o: labour rate variance
standard cost
material price variance
favourable variance
items.s: favourable variance is a difference that raises profit compared with the plan.

items.q: Which term is described by “spending that changes in total in step with the level of output”?
o: profit volume ratio
margin of safety
break even point
variable cost
items.s: variable cost is spending that changes in total in step with the level of output.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines escalation clause?
o: the rate at which workers leave and are replaced during a period
the effect of consuming more or less raw stuff than the quantity allowed for the output
the sum of direct labour and production overhead needed to turn material into finished goods
a term allowing the price to rise if input prices increase during the work
items.s: escalation clause: a term allowing the price to rise if input prices increase during the work. The other options describe conversion cost, material usage variance, labour turnover.

items.q: overhead may be defined as
o: the level of activity at which total revenue equals total spending
a proportion of the approved value held back until the work is complete
the total of all spending that cannot be traced to a single item
a pay system in which the worker receives a fixed amount for each item produced
items.s: overhead: the total of all spending that cannot be traced to a single item. The other options describe piece rate, break even point, retention money.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines budgetary control?
o: the interval between placing an order and receiving the goods
the excess of actual sales over the break even level
the practice of comparing actual results with the plan and acting on the differences
the size of the order placed each time the holding falls to the trigger point
items.s: budgetary control: the practice of comparing actual results with the plan and acting on the differences. The other options describe lead time, margin of safety, reorder quantity.

items.q: Which of the following best describes joint products?
o: the number of times the average holding is used up during a period
two or more items of significant value produced together from the same input
the total of all spending that cannot be traced to a single item
the rate at which workers leave and are replaced during a period
items.s: joint products: two or more items of significant value produced together from the same input. The other options describe overhead, labour turnover, stock turnover.

items.q: Which term is described by “the extra above the normal hourly amount paid for hours beyond the standard”?
o: time rate
idle time
direct labour
overtime premium
items.s: overtime premium is the extra above the normal hourly amount paid for hours beyond the standard.

items.q: All of the following belong to Labour and remuneration EXCEPT
o: time rate
overtime premium
piece rate
maximum level
items.s: Every other option belongs to Labour and remuneration. “maximum level” belongs to Material control and stock levels, not Labour and remuneration.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines budgetary control.
o: a proportion of the approved value held back until the work is complete
a single recovery figure applied to the whole factory instead of separate departmental ones
the amount of indirect spending recovered for each unit of the chosen base
the practice of comparing actual results with the plan and acting on the differences
items.s: budgetary control: the practice of comparing actual results with the plan and acting on the differences. The other options describe retention money, absorption rate, blanket rate.

items.q: notional profit may be defined as
o: the excess of approved value over expenditure to date on an unfinished contract
contribution expressed as a percentage of sales value
the effect of working faster or slower than the hours allowed
the value of the best alternative given up when one choice is preferred to another
items.s: notional profit: the excess of approved value over expenditure to date on an unfinished contract. The other options describe opportunity cost, labour efficiency variance, profit volume ratio.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines retention money?
o: the recovery of indirect spending into the figure carried by each product using a chosen rate
the record kept in the accounts office showing quantity and value of each item
a proportion of the approved value held back until the work is complete
the sum of direct labour and production overhead needed to turn material into finished goods
items.s: retention money: a proportion of the approved value held back until the work is complete. The other options describe stores ledger, conversion cost, absorption.

items.q: The statement “the pricing rule under which the newest consignment is treated as issued first” describes which of the following?
o: fifo
lifo
scrap value
abnormal loss
items.s: lifo is the pricing rule under which the newest consignment is treated as issued first.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines work in progress?
o: the rate at which workers leave and are replaced during a period
the value of the best alternative given up when one choice is preferred to another
goods that have started production but are not complete at the period end
the method used for large long term works carried out at the site of the customer
items.s: work in progress: goods that have started production but are not complete at the period end. The other options describe labour turnover, opportunity cost, contract costing.

items.q: All of the following belong to Nature of cost accounting EXCEPT
o: cost unit
direct expense
cost centre
piece rate
items.s: Every other option belongs to Nature of cost accounting. “piece rate” belongs to Labour and remuneration, not Nature of cost accounting.

items.q: process account may be defined as
o: the record of quantities and values entering and leaving one stage of production
the recovery of indirect spending into the figure carried by each product using a chosen rate
the recovery figure worked out for every unit of running time of a plant item
the sum of direct material, direct labour and direct outlay on a product
items.s: process account: the record of quantities and values entering and leaving one stage of production. The other options describe prime cost, machine hour rate, absorption.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines scrap value?
o: a section that supports production without working directly on the product
a term allowing the price to rise if input prices increase during the work
the pricing rule under which the newest consignment is treated as issued first
the amount obtainable by selling waste material
items.s: scrap value: the amount obtainable by selling waste material. The other options describe lifo, escalation clause, service department.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines job costing?
o: the rate at which workers leave and are replaced during a period
the method that gathers expenditure separately for each distinct order or batch
an outlay that can be traced wholly to the particular item being made
the practice of charging each issue with the exact amount paid for that consignment
items.s: job costing: the method that gathers expenditure separately for each distinct order or batch. The other options describe specific price, direct expense, labour turnover.

items.q: retention money may be defined as
o: a written plan of expected income and spending for a stated future period
the holding at which a fresh order should be placed
a proportion of the approved value held back until the work is complete
the batch size at which the cost of placing orders and the cost of keeping stock together reach their lowest
items.s: retention money: a proportion of the approved value held back until the work is complete. The other options describe reorder level, economic order quantity, budget.

items.q: The statement “the holding at which a fresh order should be placed” describes which of the following?
o: reorder level
bin card
minimum level
maximum level
items.s: reorder level is the holding at which a fresh order should be placed.

items.q: Which of the following best describes work certified?
o: the value of completed construction that the architect of the customer has approved for payment
the level of activity at which total revenue equals total spending
a predetermined figure for what an item should absorb under efficient conditions
work that can be identified with a particular product and charged to it
items.s: work certified: the value of completed construction that the architect of the customer has approved for payment. The other options describe direct labour, break even point, standard cost.

items.q: The statement “paid hours during which no production takes place because of breakdown or waiting” describes which of the following?
o: direct labour
overtime premium
idle time
gross pay
items.s: idle time is paid hours during which no production takes place because of breakdown or waiting.

items.q: Which term is described by “an outlay that can be traced wholly to the particular item being made”?
o: indirect expense
direct expense
prime cost
cost centre
items.s: direct expense is an outlay that can be traced wholly to the particular item being made.

items.q: Which of the following best describes production budget?
o: a pay system in which the worker receives a fixed amount for each hour worked
the effect of consuming more or less raw stuff than the quantity allowed for the output
the buffer quantity kept against unexpected delays in delivery
a forecast of the quantities to be made in each period
items.s: production budget: a forecast of the quantities to be made in each period. The other options describe time rate, material usage variance, minimum level.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines job costing.
o: a forecast of the quantities to be made in each period
the method that gathers expenditure separately for each distinct order or batch
contribution expressed as a percentage of sales value
a single recovery figure applied to the whole factory instead of separate departmental ones
items.s: job costing: the method that gathers expenditure separately for each distinct order or batch. The other options describe production budget, profit volume ratio, blanket rate.

items.q: indirect expense may be defined as
o: the stage at which items coming from one input become separately identifiable
a section of the business for which expenditure is gathered and charged separately
the excess of sales over variable spending, which goes towards fixed spending and profit
an outlay that cannot be traced to one item and must therefore be shared out
items.s: indirect expense: an outlay that cannot be traced to one item and must therefore be shared out. The other options describe contribution, split off point, cost centre.

items.q: The statement “the buffer quantity kept against unexpected delays in delivery” describes which of the following?
o: maximum level
minimum level
stock out
reorder quantity
items.s: minimum level is the buffer quantity kept against unexpected delays in delivery.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines lead time.
o: the size of the order placed each time the holding falls to the trigger point
the interval between placing an order and receiving the goods
the method used for large long term works carried out at the site of the customer
the situation where less indirect spending is recovered than was actually incurred
items.s: lead time: the interval between placing an order and receiving the goods. The other options describe under absorption, reorder quantity, contract costing.

items.q: The statement “a forecast of the quantities to be made in each period” describes which of the following?
o: production budget
cash budget
flexible budget
budget
items.s: production budget is a forecast of the quantities to be made in each period.

items.q: The statement “waste above the expected level, which is kept out of the cost of good output” describes which of the following?
o: weighted average price
stock turnover
abnormal loss
lifo
items.s: abnormal loss is waste above the expected level, which is kept out of the cost of good output.

items.q: lifo may be defined as
o: the batch size at which the cost of placing orders and the cost of keeping stock together reach their lowest
the pricing rule under which the oldest consignment is treated as issued first
a pay system in which the worker receives a fixed amount for each item produced
the pricing rule under which the newest consignment is treated as issued first
items.s: lifo: the pricing rule under which the newest consignment is treated as issued first. The other options describe fifo, piece rate, economic order quantity.

items.q: Which of the following best describes labour turnover?
o: the buffer quantity kept against unexpected delays in delivery
the rate at which workers leave and are replaced during a period
the value of completed construction that the architect of the customer has approved for payment
the batch size at which the cost of placing orders and the cost of keeping stock together reach their lowest
items.s: labour turnover: the rate at which workers leave and are replaced during a period. The other options describe economic order quantity, work certified, minimum level.

items.q: Which term is described by “the highest holding allowed without risking waste or excess storage charges”?
o: stores ledger
stock out
maximum level
reorder level
items.s: maximum level is the highest holding allowed without risking waste or excess storage charges.

items.q: Which of the following best describes break even point?
o: the excess of sales over variable spending, which goes towards fixed spending and profit
the level of activity at which total revenue equals total spending
the stage at which items coming from one input become separately identifiable
the difference between a planned figure and the figure actually recorded
items.s: break even point: the level of activity at which total revenue equals total spending. The other options describe split off point, variance, contribution.

items.q: Which term is described by “the record kept in the accounts office showing quantity and value of each item”?
o: reorder level
stores ledger
bin card
economic order quantity
items.s: stores ledger is the record kept in the accounts office showing quantity and value of each item.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines overtime premium?
o: the effect of paying a different hourly amount from the one planned
the extra above the normal hourly amount paid for hours beyond the standard
a term allowing the price to rise if input prices increase during the work
the pricing rule under which the newest consignment is treated as issued first
items.s: overtime premium: the extra above the normal hourly amount paid for hours beyond the standard. The other options describe labour rate variance, escalation clause, lifo.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines stock out?
o: the situation where more indirect spending is recovered than was actually incurred
the practice of charging each issue with the exact amount paid for that consignment
the record kept in the accounts office showing quantity and value of each item
a situation in which an item is needed for production but none is held
items.s: stock out: a situation in which an item is needed for production but none is held. The other options describe over absorption, stores ledger, specific price.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines flexible budget.
o: the record kept in the accounts office showing quantity and value of each item
a proportion of the approved value held back until the work is complete
the total earnings of a worker before any deductions are made
a plan restated for the level of activity actually reached
items.s: flexible budget: a plan restated for the level of activity actually reached. The other options describe gross pay, retention money, stores ledger.

items.q: material price variance may be defined as
o: the excess of sales over variable spending, which goes towards fixed spending and profit
the effect on spending of paying more or less than the planned amount for raw stuff bought
the number of times the average holding is used up during a period
the situation where less indirect spending is recovered than was actually incurred
items.s: material price variance: the effect on spending of paying more or less than the planned amount for raw stuff bought. The other options describe under absorption, stock turnover, contribution.

items.q: Which of the following best describes direct expense?
o: a forecast of money coming in and going out during the period
an outlay that can be traced wholly to the particular item being made
the effect of consuming more or less raw stuff than the quantity allowed for the output
the excess of approved value over expenditure to date on an unfinished contract
items.s: direct expense: an outlay that can be traced wholly to the particular item being made. The other options describe material usage variance, cash budget, notional profit.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines notional profit?
o: waste above the expected level, which is kept out of the cost of good output
the excess of sales over variable spending, which goes towards fixed spending and profit
the effect on spending of paying more or less than the planned amount for raw stuff bought
the excess of approved value over expenditure to date on an unfinished contract
items.s: notional profit: the excess of approved value over expenditure to date on an unfinished contract. The other options describe material price variance, abnormal loss, contribution.

items.q: The statement “a written plan of expected income and spending for a stated future period” describes which of the following?
o: flexible budget
cash budget
budgetary control
budget
items.s: budget is a written plan of expected income and spending for a stated future period.

items.q: The statement “the excess of actual sales over the break even level” describes which of the following?
o: fixed cost
relevant cost
break even point
margin of safety
items.s: margin of safety is the excess of actual sales over the break even level.

items.q: The statement “money already spent that no future decision can change” describes which of the following?
o: cost unit
sunk cost
cost centre
opportunity cost
items.s: sunk cost is money already spent that no future decision can change.

items.q: Which term is described by “an outlay that cannot be traced to one item and must therefore be shared out”?
o: overhead
cost unit
indirect expense
direct expense
items.s: indirect expense is an outlay that cannot be traced to one item and must therefore be shared out.

items.q: Which term is described by “the practice of comparing actual results with the plan and acting on the differences”?
o: cash budget
production budget
budgetary control
budget
items.s: budgetary control is the practice of comparing actual results with the plan and acting on the differences.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines notional profit.
o: a term allowing the price to rise if input prices increase during the work
the single item or measure for which an outlay figure is worked out
the excess of approved value over expenditure to date on an unfinished contract
the excess of sales over variable spending, which goes towards fixed spending and profit
items.s: notional profit: the excess of approved value over expenditure to date on an unfinished contract. The other options describe cost unit, escalation clause, contribution.

items.q: The statement “the effect of consuming more or less raw stuff than the quantity allowed for the output” describes which of the following?
o: material usage variance
labour efficiency variance
variance
labour rate variance
items.s: material usage variance is the effect of consuming more or less raw stuff than the quantity allowed for the output.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines relevant cost.
o: a future outlay that differs between the options being compared
the excess of actual sales over the break even level
the batch size at which the cost of placing orders and the cost of keeping stock together reach their lowest
a pay system in which the worker receives a fixed amount for each item produced
items.s: relevant cost: a future outlay that differs between the options being compared. The other options describe economic order quantity, piece rate, margin of safety.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines maximum level?
o: the practice of comparing actual results with the plan and acting on the differences
the approach that charges only variable spending to products and treats fixed spending as a period item
the total earnings of a worker before any deductions are made
the highest holding allowed without risking waste or excess storage charges
items.s: maximum level: the highest holding allowed without risking waste or excess storage charges. The other options describe gross pay, marginal costing, budgetary control.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines cash budget.
o: the total earnings of a worker before any deductions are made
an item of small value produced incidentally alongside the main output
a future outlay that differs between the options being compared
a forecast of money coming in and going out during the period
items.s: cash budget: a forecast of money coming in and going out during the period. The other options describe gross pay, relevant cost, by product.

items.q: Which term is described by “a future outlay that differs between the options being compared”?
o: margin of safety
break even point
relevant cost
variable cost
items.s: relevant cost is a future outlay that differs between the options being compared.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines apportionment.
o: the sharing of a common item of spending between sections on an agreed basis
the effect of working faster or slower than the hours allowed
the effect of consuming more or less raw stuff than the quantity allowed for the output
a written plan of expected income and spending for a stated future period
items.s: apportionment: the sharing of a common item of spending between sections on an agreed basis. The other options describe labour efficiency variance, budget, material usage variance.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines zero based budget.
o: a plan built from nothing so that every item must be justified afresh
the practice of comparing actual results with the plan and acting on the differences
a rate obtained by dividing the total value of goods available by the total quantity
the record of quantities and values entering and leaving one stage of production
items.s: zero based budget: a plan built from nothing so that every item must be justified afresh. The other options describe weighted average price, process account, budgetary control.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines margin of safety.
o: spending that changes in total in step with the level of output
a plan built from nothing so that every item must be justified afresh
the record of quantities and values entering and leaving one stage of production
the excess of actual sales over the break even level
items.s: margin of safety: the excess of actual sales over the break even level. The other options describe zero based budget, variable cost, process account.

items.q: Which of the following best describes marginal costing?
o: a term allowing the price to rise if input prices increase during the work
the expression of partly finished work in terms of fully finished items
the record of quantities and values entering and leaving one stage of production
the approach that charges only variable spending to products and treats fixed spending as a period item
items.s: marginal costing: the approach that charges only variable spending to products and treats fixed spending as a period item. The other options describe equivalent units, process account, escalation clause.

items.q: The statement “a term allowing the price to rise if input prices increase during the work” describes which of the following?
o: notional profit
retention money
escalation clause
job costing
items.s: escalation clause is a term allowing the price to rise if input prices increase during the work.

items.q: The cost of goods sold in a year was 480000 naira. Opening stock was 60000 naira and closing stock was 140000 naira. What is the stock turnover rate?
A store held 200 units at 10 naira each and then received 300 units at 22 naira each. 150 units were issued immediately afterwards. Using LIFO, what is the value of the issue?
items.s: LIFO takes the newest units first: 150 x 22 = 3300 naira.

items.q: A store held 300 units at 16 naira each and received 200 units at 24 naira each. What is the weighted average price per unit?
items.s: Weighted average = (300 x 16 + 200 x 24)/(300 + 200) = 19.2 naira.

items.q: A worker is paid 750 naira an hour for a standard week of 200 hours and one and a half times that for overtime. He worked 15 hours of overtime. What is his gross pay?
items.s: Gross pay = 200 x 750 + 15 x 750 x 1.5 = 166875 naira.

items.q: A department expects to incur 540000 naira of overheads and to run its machines for 1200 hours. What is the machine hour rate?
items.s: Machine hour rate = overheads/machine hours = 540000/1200 = 450 naira per hour.

items.q: A product sells for 150 naira a unit and has variable costs of 70 naira a unit. Fixed costs are 60000 naira a period and 1500 units are sold. What is the profit?
items.s: Profit = (selling price - variable cost) x units - fixed costs = (150 - 70) x 1500 - 60000 = 60000 naira.

items.q: A cash budget opens with a balance of 220000 naira. Receipts for the month are 360000 naira and payments are 180000 naira. What is the closing balance?
items.s: Closing balance = opening balance + receipts - payments = 220000 + 360000 - 180000 = 400000 naira.

items.q: A firm bought and used 5000 kg of material. The standard price was 20 naira a kg and the actual price was 17 naira a kg. What is the material price variance?
items.s: Price variance = (standard price - actual price) x quantity = (20 - 17) x 5000 = 15000 naira.

items.q: A batch uses 48000 naira of material, 44000 naira of direct labour and 9000 naira of direct expenses. What is the prime cost?
items.s: Prime cost = material + direct labour + direct expenses = 48000 + 44000 + 9000 = 101000 naira.

items.q: Fixed spending is 120000 naira a period and variable spending is 45 naira per unit. What is the total cost of 4000 units?
items.s: Total cost = fixed + variable x units = 120000 + 45 x 4000 = 300000 naira.

items.q: A firm uses 16000 units of an item a year. Each order costs 50 naira to place and holding costs 8 naira per unit a year. What is the economic order quantity?
items.s: EOQ = square root of (2 x annual demand x ordering cost / holding cost) = square root of (2 x 16000 x 50 / 8) = 447.21 units.

items.q: An item is used at a maximum of 400 units a week and the longest delivery delay is 2 weeks. What reorder level should be set?
items.s: Reorder level = maximum usage x maximum lead time = 400 x 2 = 800 units.

items.q: The reorder level of an item is 3000 units and the reorder quantity is 1000 units. Minimum usage is 200 units a week over a minimum lead time of 2 weeks. What is the maximum stock level?
items.s: Maximum level = reorder level + reorder quantity - (minimum usage x minimum lead time) = 3000 + 1000 - 200 x 2 = 3600 units.

items.q: The reorder level of an item is 4200 units. Average usage is 400 units a week and the average lead time is 4 weeks. What is the minimum stock level?
items.s: Minimum level = reorder level - (average usage x average lead time) = 4200 - 400 x 4 = 2600 units.

items.q: A store held 300 units at 20 naira each and then received 300 units at 26 naira each. 400 units were issued. Using FIFO, what is the value of the issue?
items.s: FIFO takes the oldest units first: 300 x 20 + 100 x 26 = 8600 naira.

items.q: Workers put in 600 hours at 500 naira an hour to make 800 units. What is the labour cost per unit?
items.s: Labour cost per unit = (600 x 500)/800 = 375 naira.

items.q: Budgeted overheads are 900000 naira for 20000 budgeted hours. Actual hours worked were 16000 and actual overheads were 900000 naira. Taking absorbed minus incurred, what is the over or under absorption figure?
items.s: Absorption rate = 900000/20000 = 45 per hour; absorbed = 45 x 16000 = 720000; figure = absorbed - incurred = 720000 - 900000 = -180000 naira, an amount of under absorption.

items.q: Rent of 480000 naira is shared between three departments in the ratio 3:3:2 by floor area. What amount is charged to the first department?
items.s: Share = total x ratio/total ratio = 480000 x 3/8 = 180000 naira.

items.q: A job used 180000 naira of material, 110000 naira of labour and 90000 naira of overheads. The firm quotes a price with a profit of 25 percent on total cost. What is the price?
The value of work certified on an unfinished contract is 1300000 naira and the cost incurred to date is 700000 naira. What is the notional profit?
items.s: Notional profit = value certified - cost to date = 1300000 - 700000 = 600000 naira.

items.q: A process takes in 8000 units at a total cost of 720000 naira. Normal loss is 5 percent of input and the loss sells for 2 naira a unit. What is the cost per good unit?
items.s: Normal loss = 400 units worth 800 naira; cost per good unit = (720000 - 800)/(8000 - 400) = 94.63 naira.

items.q: A process put in 5000 units. Normal loss is 10 percent of input and actual output was 4200 units. What is the number of abnormal loss units?
items.s: Expected output = 5000 - 500 = 4500 units; abnormal loss = 4500 - 4200 = 300 units.

items.q: Fixed costs are 180000 naira a period. Each unit sells for 100 naira and has a variable cost of 70 naira. What is the break even point in units?
items.s: Break even units = fixed costs/contribution per unit = 180000/(100 - 70) = 6000 units.

items.q: A firm sells 8000 units against a break even volume of 4000 units. Each unit sells for 100 naira. What is the margin of safety in naira?
items.s: Margin of safety = (8000 - 4000) x 100 = 400000 naira.

items.q: A product sells for 160 naira a unit and its variable cost is 96 naira a unit. What is the profit volume ratio?
items.s: Profit volume ratio = (selling price - variable cost)/selling price x 100 = (160 - 96)/160 x 100 = 40 percent.

items.q: Fixed costs are 160000 naira and the firm wants a profit of 80000 naira. Each unit contributes 25 naira. How many units must be sold?
items.s: Units = (fixed costs + target profit)/contribution per unit = (160000 + 80000)/25 = 9600 units.

items.q: Budgeted sales are 4000 units. Opening stock is 800 units and the firm wants 600 units left at the end. How many units must be produced?
items.s: Production = sales + closing stock - opening stock = 4000 + 600 - 800 = 3800 units.

items.q: Production was 2500 units. The standard allowance is 5 kg a unit and 8 kg a unit were actually used. Material is valued at 12 naira a kg. What is the material usage variance?
items.s: Usage variance = (standard quantity - actual quantity) x standard price = (12500 - 20000) x 12 = -90000 naira.

items.q: Workers worked 3000 hours. The standard rate was 400 naira an hour and the actual rate paid was 450 naira an hour. What is the labour rate variance?
items.s: Rate variance = (standard rate - actual rate) x hours = (400 - 450) x 3000 = -150000 naira.

items.q: A firm made 1000 units. The standard time allowed is 4 hours a unit and 5 hours a unit were actually worked. The standard rate is 300 naira an hour. What is the labour efficiency variance?
items.s: Efficiency variance = (standard hours - actual hours) x standard rate = (4000 - 5000) x 300 = -300000 naira.

items.q: A factory produced 2000 units in a period and incurred 240000 naira of material, 210000 naira of labour and 150000 naira of overheads. What is the cost per unit?
The cost of goods sold in a year was 480000 naira. Opening stock was 90000 naira and closing stock was 140000 naira. What is the stock turnover rate?
A store held 200 units at 10 naira each and then received 300 units at 22 naira each. 300 units were issued immediately afterwards. Using LIFO, what is the value of the issue?
items.s: LIFO takes the newest units first: 300 x 22 = 6600 naira.

items.q: A store held 300 units at 12 naira each and received 100 units at 26 naira each. What is the weighted average price per unit?
items.s: Weighted average = (300 x 12 + 100 x 26)/(300 + 100) = 15.5 naira.

items.q: A worker is paid 750 naira an hour for a standard week of 160 hours and one and a half times that for overtime. He worked 20 hours of overtime. What is his gross pay?
items.s: Gross pay = 160 x 750 + 20 x 750 x 1.5 = 142500 naira.

items.q: Budgeted overheads for a year are 600000 naira and budgeted labour hours are 15000. What is the overhead absorption rate per labour hour?
items.s: Absorption rate = budgeted overheads/budgeted hours = 600000/15000 = 40 naira per hour.

items.q: A department expects to incur 360000 naira of overheads and to run its machines for 2700 hours. What is the machine hour rate?
items.s: Machine hour rate = overheads/machine hours = 360000/2700 = 133.33 naira per hour.

items.q: Work certified on a contract to date is 800000 naira and the contract provides for retention of 15 percent. What amount is held back?
items.s: Retention = 800000 x 15/100 = 120000 naira.

items.q: A product sells for 120 naira a unit and has variable costs of 70 naira a unit. Fixed costs are 60000 naira a period and 1500 units are sold. What is the profit?
items.s: Profit = (selling price - variable cost) x units - fixed costs = (120 - 70) x 1500 - 60000 = 15000 naira.

items.q: Fixed costs are 240000 naira a period and the contribution to sales ratio is 40 percent. What is the break even sales revenue?
items.s: Break even revenue = fixed costs/contribution ratio = 240000/0.4 = 600000 naira.

items.q: A cash budget opens with a balance of 150000 naira. Receipts for the month are 360000 naira and payments are 290000 naira. What is the closing balance?
items.s: Closing balance = opening balance + receipts - payments = 150000 + 360000 - 290000 = 220000 naira.

items.q: A firm bought and used 2000 kg of material. The standard price was 20 naira a kg and the actual price was 17 naira a kg. What is the material price variance?
items.s: Price variance = (standard price - actual price) x quantity = (20 - 17) x 2000 = 6000 naira.

items.q: A batch uses 75000 naira of material, 44000 naira of direct labour and 9000 naira of direct expenses. What is the prime cost?
items.s: Prime cost = material + direct labour + direct expenses = 75000 + 44000 + 9000 = 128000 naira.

items.q: Fixed spending is 240000 naira a period and variable spending is 45 naira per unit. What is the total cost of 5000 units?
items.s: Total cost = fixed + variable x units = 240000 + 45 x 5000 = 465000 naira.

items.q: A firm uses 16000 units of an item a year. Each order costs 40 naira to place and holding costs 8 naira per unit a year. What is the economic order quantity?
items.s: EOQ = square root of (2 x annual demand x ordering cost / holding cost) = square root of (2 x 16000 x 40 / 8) = 400 units.

items.q: The reorder level of an item is 3600 units and the reorder quantity is 1500 units. Minimum usage is 300 units a week over a minimum lead time of 2 weeks. What is the maximum stock level?
items.s: Maximum level = reorder level + reorder quantity - (minimum usage x minimum lead time) = 3600 + 1500 - 300 x 2 = 4500 units.

items.q: The reorder level of an item is 4200 units. Average usage is 500 units a week and the average lead time is 3 weeks. What is the minimum stock level?
items.s: Minimum level = reorder level - (average usage x average lead time) = 4200 - 500 x 3 = 2700 units.

items.q: A store held 100 units at 12 naira each and then received 300 units at 30 naira each. 250 units were issued. Using FIFO, what is the value of the issue?
items.s: FIFO takes the oldest units first: 100 x 12 + 150 x 30 = 5700 naira.

items.q: A worker earning 550 naira an hour worked 16 hours of overtime at time and a half. What is the overtime premium charged to overhead?
items.s: Premium = overtime hours x hourly rate x 0.5 = 16 x 550 x 0.5 = 4400 naira.

items.q: Workers put in 900 hours at 500 naira an hour to make 600 units. What is the labour cost per unit?
items.s: Labour cost per unit = (900 x 500)/600 = 750 naira.

items.q: Budgeted overheads are 1200000 naira for 15000 budgeted hours. Actual hours worked were 16000 and actual overheads were 1200000 naira. Taking absorbed minus incurred, what is the over or under absorption figure?
items.s: Absorption rate = 1200000/15000 = 80 per hour; absorbed = 80 x 16000 = 1280000; figure = absorbed - incurred = 1280000 - 1200000 = 80000 naira, an amount of over absorption.

items.q: Rent of 720000 naira is shared between three departments in the ratio 4:2:1 by floor area. What amount is charged to the first department?
items.s: Share = total x ratio/total ratio = 720000 x 4/7 = 411428.57 naira.

items.q: A job used 120000 naira of material, 110000 naira of labour and 40000 naira of overheads. The firm quotes a price with a profit of 20 percent on total cost. What is the price?
A process takes in 5000 units at a total cost of 960000 naira. Normal loss is 10 percent of input and the loss sells for 8 naira a unit. What is the cost per good unit?
items.s: Normal loss = 500 units worth 4000 naira; cost per good unit = (960000 - 4000)/(5000 - 500) = 212.44 naira.

items.q: Fixed costs are 120000 naira a period. Each unit sells for 100 naira and has a variable cost of 40 naira. What is the break even point in units?
items.s: Break even units = fixed costs/contribution per unit = 120000/(100 - 40) = 2000 units.

items.q: A firm sells 6000 units against a break even volume of 3000 units. Each unit sells for 100 naira. What is the margin of safety in naira?
items.s: Margin of safety = (6000 - 3000) x 100 = 300000 naira.

items.q: A product sells for 200 naira a unit and its variable cost is 96 naira a unit. What is the profit volume ratio?
items.s: Profit volume ratio = (selling price - variable cost)/selling price x 100 = (200 - 96)/200 x 100 = 52 percent.

items.q: Fixed costs are 100000 naira and the firm wants a profit of 120000 naira. Each unit contributes 25 naira. How many units must be sold?
items.s: Units = (fixed costs + target profit)/contribution per unit = (100000 + 120000)/25 = 8800 units.

items.q: Budgeted sales are 9000 units. Opening stock is 800 units and the firm wants 1500 units left at the end. How many units must be produced?
items.s: Production = sales + closing stock - opening stock = 9000 + 1500 - 800 = 9700 units.

items.q: Production was 2500 units. The standard allowance is 4 kg a unit and 6 kg a unit were actually used. Material is valued at 15 naira a kg. What is the material usage variance?
items.s: Usage variance = (standard quantity - actual quantity) x standard price = (10000 - 15000) x 15 = -75000 naira.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what normal loss means.
o: the pricing rule under which the newest consignment is treated as issued first
waste above the expected level, which is kept out of the cost of good output
the pricing rule under which the oldest consignment is treated as issued first
the unavoidable waste expected in a process under ordinary working conditions
items.s: normal loss: the unavoidable waste expected in a process under ordinary working conditions. The other options describe fifo, abnormal loss, lifo.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what process account means.
o: the record that carries away the expected waste at its saleable amount
goods that have started production but are not complete at the period end
the record of quantities and values entering and leaving one stage of production
an item of small value produced incidentally alongside the main output
items.s: process account: the record of quantities and values entering and leaving one stage of production. The other options describe by product, normal loss account, work in progress.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what cost centre means.
o: an outlay that cannot be traced to one item and must therefore be shared out
the single item or measure for which an outlay figure is worked out
the value of the best alternative given up when one choice is preferred to another
a section of the business for which expenditure is gathered and charged separately
items.s: cost centre: a section of the business for which expenditure is gathered and charged separately. The other options describe indirect expense, cost unit, opportunity cost.

items.q: The best definition of absorption rate among these is
o: the recovery of indirect spending into the figure carried by each product using a chosen rate
the recovery figure worked out for every unit of running time of a plant item
the amount of indirect spending recovered for each unit of the chosen base
a single recovery figure applied to the whole factory instead of separate departmental ones
items.s: absorption rate: the amount of indirect spending recovered for each unit of the chosen base. The other options describe machine hour rate, absorption, blanket rate.

items.q: The best definition of marginal costing among these is
o: contribution expressed as a percentage of sales value
the excess of sales over variable spending, which goes towards fixed spending and profit
the level of activity at which total revenue equals total spending
the approach that charges only variable spending to products and treats fixed spending as a period item
items.s: marginal costing: the approach that charges only variable spending to products and treats fixed spending as a period item. The other options describe profit volume ratio, contribution, break even point.

items.q: In this course, gross pay refers to
o: work that can be identified with a particular product and charged to it
the total earnings of a worker before any deductions are made
a pay system in which the worker receives a fixed amount for each hour worked
the rate at which workers leave and are replaced during a period
items.s: gross pay: the total earnings of a worker before any deductions are made. The other options describe labour turnover, direct labour, time rate.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the recovery figure worked out for every unit of running time of a plant item”
o: service department
allocation
absorption
machine hour rate
items.s: machine hour rate is the recovery figure worked out for every unit of running time of a plant item.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what work certified means.
o: a term allowing the price to rise if input prices increase during the work
the method that gathers expenditure separately for each distinct order or batch
a proportion of the approved value held back until the work is complete
the value of completed construction that the architect of the customer has approved for payment
items.s: work certified: the value of completed construction that the architect of the customer has approved for payment. The other options describe job costing, escalation clause, retention money.

items.q: The best definition of contract costing among these is
o: the method used for large long term works carried out at the site of the customer
a term allowing the price to rise if input prices increase during the work
a proportion of the approved value held back until the work is complete
the method that gathers expenditure separately for each distinct order or batch
items.s: contract costing: the method used for large long term works carried out at the site of the customer. The other options describe escalation clause, job costing, retention money.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the record of quantities and values entering and leaving one stage of production”
o: split off point
process account
by product
work in progress
items.s: process account is the record of quantities and values entering and leaving one stage of production.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the situation where less indirect spending is recovered than was actually incurred”
o: over absorption
absorption
under absorption
machine hour rate
items.s: under absorption is the situation where less indirect spending is recovered than was actually incurred.

items.q: Which term is described by “the method that gathers expenditure separately for each distinct order or batch”?
o: contract costing
escalation clause
job costing
work certified
items.s: job costing is the method that gathers expenditure separately for each distinct order or batch.

items.q: Which term is described by “the interval between placing an order and receiving the goods”?
o: bin card
lead time
minimum level
economic order quantity
items.s: lead time is the interval between placing an order and receiving the goods.

items.q: The statement “the extra above the normal hourly amount paid for hours beyond the standard” describes which of the following?
o: gross pay
net pay
overtime premium
piece rate
items.s: overtime premium is the extra above the normal hourly amount paid for hours beyond the standard.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what apportionment means.
o: the charging of a whole item of spending to the one section that caused it
the situation where more indirect spending is recovered than was actually incurred

items.q: The reorder level of an item is 3000 units. Average usage is 400 units a week and the average lead time is 3 weeks. What is the minimum stock level?
items.s: Minimum level = reorder level - (average usage x average lead time) = 3000 - 400 x 3 = 1800 units.

items.q: A store held 300 units at 20 naira each and then received 400 units at 30 naira each. 350 units were issued. Using FIFO, what is the value of the issue?
items.s: FIFO takes the oldest units first: 300 x 20 + 50 x 30 = 7500 naira.

items.q: A worker earning 700 naira an hour worked 12 hours of overtime at time and a half. What is the overtime premium charged to overhead?
items.s: Premium = overtime hours x hourly rate x 0.5 = 12 x 700 x 0.5 = 4200 naira.

items.q: A job used 250000 naira of material, 80000 naira of labour and 90000 naira of overheads. The firm quotes a price with a profit of 30 percent on total cost. What is the price?
A process finished and transferred 6000 units and left 800 units in progress which are 25 percent complete. What are the equivalent units of production?
items.s: Equivalent units = completed + closing work in progress x degree of completion = 6000 + 800 x 25/100 = 6200 units.

items.q: A process put in 5000 units. Normal loss is 5 percent of input and actual output was 3400 units. What is the number of abnormal loss units?
items.s: Expected output = 5000 - 250 = 4750 units; abnormal loss = 4750 - 3400 = 1350 units.

items.q: A firm sells 6000 units against a break even volume of 4000 units. Each unit sells for 120 naira. What is the margin of safety in naira?
items.s: Margin of safety = (6000 - 4000) x 120 = 240000 naira.

items.q: A product sells for 160 naira a unit and its variable cost is 120 naira a unit. What is the profit volume ratio?
items.s: Profit volume ratio = (selling price - variable cost)/selling price x 100 = (160 - 120)/160 x 100 = 25 percent.

items.q: Production was 2000 units. The standard allowance is 6 kg a unit and 8 kg a unit were actually used. Material is valued at 15 naira a kg. What is the material usage variance?
items.s: Usage variance = (standard quantity - actual quantity) x standard price = (12000 - 16000) x 15 = -60000 naira.

items.q: Workers worked 1200 hours. The standard rate was 300 naira an hour and the actual rate paid was 540 naira an hour. What is the labour rate variance?
items.s: Rate variance = (standard rate - actual rate) x hours = (300 - 540) x 1200 = -288000 naira.

items.q: A batch uses 48000 naira of material, 44000 naira of direct labour and 12000 naira of direct expenses. What is the prime cost?
items.s: Prime cost = material + direct labour + direct expenses = 48000 + 44000 + 12000 = 104000 naira.

items.q: A factory produced 2500 units in a period and incurred 480000 naira of material, 150000 naira of labour and 80000 naira of overheads. What is the cost per unit?
Fixed spending is 180000 naira a period and variable spending is 25 naira per unit. What is the total cost of 4000 units?
items.s: Total cost = fixed + variable x units = 180000 + 25 x 4000 = 280000 naira.

items.q: An item is used at a maximum of 750 units a week and the longest delivery delay is 2 weeks. What reorder level should be set?
items.s: Reorder level = maximum usage x maximum lead time = 750 x 2 = 1500 units.

items.q: The reorder level of an item is 3600 units and the reorder quantity is 1000 units. Minimum usage is 300 units a week over a minimum lead time of 3 weeks. What is the maximum stock level?
items.s: Maximum level = reorder level + reorder quantity - (minimum usage x minimum lead time) = 3600 + 1000 - 300 x 3 = 3700 units.

items.q: The cost of goods sold in a year was 900000 naira. Opening stock was 60000 naira and closing stock was 110000 naira. What is the stock turnover rate?
A store held 200 units at 10 naira each and then received 400 units at 22 naira each. 300 units were issued immediately afterwards. Using LIFO, what is the value of the issue?
items.s: LIFO takes the newest units first: 300 x 22 = 6600 naira.

items.q: A store held 200 units at 20 naira each and received 200 units at 30 naira each. What is the weighted average price per unit?
items.s: Weighted average = (200 x 20 + 200 x 30)/(200 + 200) = 25 naira.

items.q: A worker is paid 450 naira an hour for a standard week of 180 hours and one and a half times that for overtime. He worked 15 hours of overtime. What is his gross pay?
items.s: Gross pay = 180 x 450 + 15 x 450 x 1.5 = 91125 naira.

items.q: Workers put in 600 hours at 420 naira an hour to make 400 units. What is the labour cost per unit?
items.s: Labour cost per unit = (600 x 420)/400 = 630 naira.

items.q: Rent of 960000 naira is shared between three departments in the ratio 3:3:2 by floor area. What amount is charged to the first department?
items.s: Share = total x ratio/total ratio = 960000 x 3/8 = 360000 naira.

items.q: Work certified on a contract to date is 1200000 naira and the contract provides for retention of 5 percent. What amount is held back?
items.s: Retention = 1200000 x 5/100 = 60000 naira.

items.s: Normal loss = 500 units worth 2500 naira; cost per good unit = (720000 - 2500)/(10000 - 500) = 75.53 naira.

items.q: A product sells for 120 naira a unit and has variable costs of 110 naira a unit. Fixed costs are 60000 naira a period and 2000 units are sold. What is the profit?
items.s: Profit = (selling price - variable cost) x units - fixed costs = (120 - 110) x 2000 - 60000 = -40000 naira.

items.q: Fixed costs are 120000 naira a period. Each unit sells for 150 naira and has a variable cost of 40 naira. What is the break even point in units?

items.s: Units = (fixed costs + target profit)/contribution per unit = (100000 + 120000)/40 = 5500 units.

items.s: LIFO takes the newest units first: 250 x 32 = 8000 naira.

items.q: A worker is paid 450 naira an hour for a standard week of 160 hours and one and a half times that for overtime. He worked 20 hours of overtime. What is his gross pay?
items.s: Gross pay = 160 x 450 + 20 x 450 x 1.5 = 85500 naira.

items.q: Workers put in 900 hours at 350 naira an hour to make 600 units. What is the labour cost per unit?
items.s: Labour cost per unit = (900 x 350)/600 = 525 naira.

items.q: Budgeted overheads for a year are 1200000 naira and budgeted labour hours are 20000. What is the overhead absorption rate per labour hour?
items.s: Absorption rate = budgeted overheads/budgeted hours = 1200000/20000 = 60 naira per hour.

items.q: Rent of 720000 naira is shared between three departments in the ratio 3:4:3 by floor area. What amount is charged to the first department?
items.s: Share = total x ratio/total ratio = 720000 x 3/10 = 216000 naira.

items.q: A department expects to incur 540000 naira of overheads and to run its machines for 1800 hours. What is the machine hour rate?
items.s: Machine hour rate = overheads/machine hours = 540000/1800 = 300 naira per hour.

items.q: A process takes in 8000 units at a total cost of 960000 naira. Normal loss is 10 percent of input and the loss sells for 8 naira a unit. What is the cost per good unit?
items.s: Normal loss = 800 units worth 6400 naira; cost per good unit = (960000 - 6400)/(8000 - 800) = 132.44 naira.

items.q: Fixed costs are 180000 naira a period. Each unit sells for 150 naira and has a variable cost of 40 naira. What is the break even point in units?
items.s: Break even units = fixed costs/contribution per unit = 180000/(150 - 40) = 1636.36 units.

items.q: Fixed costs are 150000 naira a period and the contribution to sales ratio is 40 percent. What is the break even sales revenue?
items.s: Break even revenue = fixed costs/contribution ratio = 150000/0.4 = 375000 naira.

items.q: Fixed costs are 160000 naira and the firm wants a profit of 120000 naira. Each unit contributes 25 naira. How many units must be sold?
items.s: Units = (fixed costs + target profit)/contribution per unit = (160000 + 120000)/25 = 11200 units.

items.q: Budgeted sales are 6000 units. Opening stock is 800 units and the firm wants 600 units left at the end. How many units must be produced?
items.s: Production = sales + closing stock - opening stock = 6000 + 600 - 800 = 5800 units.

items.q: A cash budget opens with a balance of 220000 naira. Receipts for the month are 240000 naira and payments are 290000 naira. What is the closing balance?
items.s: Closing balance = opening balance + receipts - payments = 220000 + 240000 - 290000 = 170000 naira.

items.q: A firm made 500 units. The standard time allowed is 2 hours a unit and 6 hours a unit were actually worked. The standard rate is 250 naira an hour. What is the labour efficiency variance?
items.s: Efficiency variance = (standard hours - actual hours) x standard rate = (1000 - 3000) x 250 = -500000 naira.

items.q: A firm uses 9000 units of an item a year. Each order costs 90 naira to place and holding costs 5 naira per unit a year. What is the economic order quantity?
items.s: EOQ = square root of (2 x annual demand x ordering cost / holding cost) = square root of (2 x 9000 x 90 / 5) = 569.21 units.

items.q: The reorder level of an item is 5400 units. Average usage is 500 units a week and the average lead time is 4 weeks. What is the minimum stock level?
items.s: Minimum level = reorder level - (average usage x average lead time) = 5400 - 500 x 4 = 3400 units.

items.q: A store held 100 units at 15 naira each and then received 300 units at 26 naira each. 250 units were issued. Using FIFO, what is the value of the issue?
items.s: FIFO takes the oldest units first: 100 x 15 + 150 x 26 = 5400 naira.

items.q: Budgeted overheads are 600000 naira for 20000 budgeted hours. Actual hours worked were 28000 and actual overheads were 600000 naira. Taking absorbed minus incurred, what is the over or under absorption figure?
items.s: Absorption rate = 600000/20000 = 30 per hour; absorbed = 30 x 28000 = 840000; figure = absorbed - incurred = 840000 - 600000 = 240000 naira, an amount of over absorption.

items.q: A process takes in 10000 units at a total cost of 450000 naira. Normal loss is 10 percent of input and the loss sells for 5 naira a unit. What is the cost per good unit?
items.s: Normal loss = 1000 units worth 5000 naira; cost per good unit = (450000 - 5000)/(10000 - 1000) = 49.44 naira.

items.q: Fixed costs are 160000 naira and the firm wants a profit of 50000 naira. Each unit contributes 25 naira. How many units must be sold?
items.s: Units = (fixed costs + target profit)/contribution per unit = (160000 + 50000)/25 = 8400 units.

items.q: A firm made 800 units. The standard time allowed is 3 hours a unit and 6 hours a unit were actually worked. The standard rate is 250 naira an hour. What is the labour efficiency variance?
items.s: Efficiency variance = (standard hours - actual hours) x standard rate = (2400 - 4800) x 250 = -600000 naira.

items.q: A batch uses 75000 naira of material, 30000 naira of direct labour and 12000 naira of direct expenses. What is the prime cost?
items.s: Prime cost = material + direct labour + direct expenses = 75000 + 30000 + 12000 = 117000 naira.
