A firm uses 9000 units of an item a year. Each order costs 90 naira to place and holding costs 2 naira per unit a year. What is the economic order quantity?
items.s: EOQ = square root of (2 x annual demand x ordering cost / holding cost) = square root of (2 x 9000 x 90 / 2) = 900 units.

items.q: An item is used at a maximum of 750 units a week and the longest delivery delay is 3 weeks. What reorder level should be set?
items.s: Reorder level = maximum usage x maximum lead time = 750 x 3 = 2250 units.

items.q: The reorder level of an item is 4200 units. Average usage is 500 units a week and the average lead time is 4 weeks. What is the minimum stock level?
items.s: Minimum level = reorder level - (average usage x average lead time) = 4200 - 500 x 4 = 2200 units.

items.q: The cost of goods sold in a year was 720000 naira. Opening stock was 90000 naira and closing stock was 140000 naira. What is the stock turnover rate?
A store held 300 units at 15 naira each and then received 300 units at 24 naira each. 400 units were issued. Using FIFO, what is the value of the issue?
items.s: FIFO takes the oldest units first: 300 x 15 + 100 x 24 = 6900 naira.

items.q: A store held 200 units at 14 naira each and then received 300 units at 28 naira each. 250 units were issued immediately afterwards. Using LIFO, what is the value of the issue?
items.s: LIFO takes the newest units first: 250 x 28 = 7000 naira.

items.q: A store held 400 units at 16 naira each and received 300 units at 30 naira each. What is the weighted average price per unit?
items.s: Weighted average = (400 x 16 + 300 x 30)/(400 + 300) = 22 naira.

items.q: A worker is paid 600 naira an hour for a standard week of 180 hours and one and a half times that for overtime. He worked 15 hours of overtime. What is his gross pay?
items.s: Gross pay = 180 x 600 + 15 x 600 x 1.5 = 121500 naira.

items.q: Workers put in 600 hours at 350 naira an hour to make 400 units. What is the labour cost per unit?
items.s: Labour cost per unit = (600 x 350)/400 = 525 naira.

items.q: Rent of 480000 naira is shared between three departments in the ratio 4:2:1 by floor area. What amount is charged to the first department?
items.s: Share = total x ratio/total ratio = 480000 x 4/7 = 274285.71 naira.

items.q: A department expects to incur 810000 naira of overheads and to run its machines for 2700 hours. What is the machine hour rate?
items.s: Machine hour rate = overheads/machine hours = 810000/2700 = 300 naira per hour.

items.q: A job used 180000 naira of material, 150000 naira of labour and 90000 naira of overheads. The firm quotes a price with a profit of 20 percent on total cost. What is the price?
Work certified on a contract to date is 1500000 naira and the contract provides for retention of 15 percent. What amount is held back?
items.s: Retention = 1500000 x 15/100 = 225000 naira.

items.q: A process finished and transferred 6000 units and left 1600 units in progress which are 50 percent complete. What are the equivalent units of production?
items.s: Equivalent units = completed + closing work in progress x degree of completion = 6000 + 1600 x 50/100 = 6800 units.

items.q: A process put in 8000 units. Normal loss is 10 percent of input and actual output was 7000 units. What is the number of abnormal loss units?
items.s: Expected output = 8000 - 800 = 7200 units; abnormal loss = 7200 - 7000 = 200 units.

items.q: A product sells for 200 naira a unit and has variable costs of 90 naira a unit. Fixed costs are 60000 naira a period and 1500 units are sold. What is the profit?
items.s: Profit = (selling price - variable cost) x units - fixed costs = (200 - 90) x 1500 - 60000 = 105000 naira.

items.q: Fixed costs are 120000 naira a period. Each unit sells for 100 naira and has a variable cost of 55 naira. What is the break even point in units?
items.s: Break even units = fixed costs/contribution per unit = 120000/(100 - 55) = 2666.67 units.

items.q: A firm sells 5000 units against a break even volume of 5000 units. Each unit sells for 120 naira. What is the margin of safety in naira?
items.s: Margin of safety = (5000 - 5000) x 120 = 0 naira.

items.q: Budgeted sales are 4000 units. Opening stock is 500 units and the firm wants 900 units left at the end. How many units must be produced?
items.s: Production = sales + closing stock - opening stock = 4000 + 900 - 500 = 4400 units.

items.q: A cash budget opens with a balance of 80000 naira. Receipts for the month are 360000 naira and payments are 290000 naira. What is the closing balance?
items.s: Closing balance = opening balance + receipts - payments = 80000 + 360000 - 290000 = 150000 naira.

items.q: A firm bought and used 5000 kg of material. The standard price was 12 naira a kg and the actual price was 22 naira a kg. What is the material price variance?
items.s: Price variance = (standard price - actual price) x quantity = (12 - 22) x 5000 = -50000 naira.

items.q: Workers worked 2000 hours. The standard rate was 400 naira an hour and the actual rate paid was 540 naira an hour. What is the labour rate variance?
items.s: Rate variance = (standard rate - actual rate) x hours = (400 - 540) x 2000 = -280000 naira.

items.q: The reorder level of an item is 2400 units and the reorder quantity is 1000 units. Minimum usage is 300 units a week over a minimum lead time of 3 weeks. What is the maximum stock level?
items.s: Maximum level = reorder level + reorder quantity - (minimum usage x minimum lead time) = 2400 + 1000 - 300 x 3 = 2500 units.

items.q: Budgeted overheads are 1200000 naira for 20000 budgeted hours. Actual hours worked were 28000 and actual overheads were 1200000 naira. Taking absorbed minus incurred, what is the over or under absorption figure?
items.s: Absorption rate = 1200000/20000 = 60 per hour; absorbed = 60 x 28000 = 1680000; figure = absorbed - incurred = 1680000 - 1200000 = 480000 naira, an amount of over absorption.

items.q: A process takes in 8000 units at a total cost of 720000 naira. Normal loss is 5 percent of input and the loss sells for 5 naira a unit. What is the cost per good unit?
items.s: Normal loss = 400 units worth 2000 naira; cost per good unit = (720000 - 2000)/(8000 - 400) = 94.47 naira.

items.q: Fixed costs are 160000 naira and the firm wants a profit of 120000 naira. Each unit contributes 20 naira. How many units must be sold?
items.s: Units = (fixed costs + target profit)/contribution per unit = (160000 + 120000)/20 = 14000 units.

items.q: A firm made 800 units. The standard time allowed is 4 hours a unit and 6 hours a unit were actually worked. The standard rate is 250 naira an hour. What is the labour efficiency variance?
items.s: Efficiency variance = (standard hours - actual hours) x standard rate = (3200 - 4800) x 250 = -400000 naira.

items.q: A factory produced 4000 units in a period and incurred 360000 naira of material, 150000 naira of labour and 80000 naira of overheads. What is the cost per unit?
Fixed spending is 120000 naira a period and variable spending is 32 naira per unit. What is the total cost of 4000 units?
items.s: Total cost = fixed + variable x units = 120000 + 32 x 4000 = 248000 naira.

items.q: A firm uses 9000 units of an item a year. Each order costs 50 naira to place and holding costs 5 naira per unit a year. What is the economic order quantity?
items.s: EOQ = square root of (2 x annual demand x ordering cost / holding cost) = square root of (2 x 9000 x 50 / 5) = 424.26 units.

items.q: The cost of goods sold in a year was 720000 naira. Opening stock was 60000 naira and closing stock was 140000 naira. What is the stock turnover rate?
A store held 200 units at 20 naira each and then received 200 units at 30 naira each. 350 units were issued. Using FIFO, what is the value of the issue?
items.s: FIFO takes the oldest units first: 200 x 20 + 150 x 30 = 8500 naira.

items.q: A store held 100 units at 18 naira each and then received 300 units at 28 naira each. 150 units were issued immediately afterwards. Using LIFO, what is the value of the issue?
items.s: LIFO takes the newest units first: 150 x 28 = 4200 naira.

items.q: A store held 400 units at 20 naira each and received 200 units at 24 naira each. What is the weighted average price per unit?
items.s: Weighted average = (400 x 20 + 200 x 24)/(400 + 200) = 21.33 naira.

items.q: A worker is paid 450 naira an hour for a standard week of 180 hours and one and a half times that for overtime. He worked 20 hours of overtime. What is his gross pay?
items.s: Gross pay = 180 x 450 + 20 x 450 x 1.5 = 94500 naira.

items.q: Workers put in 1200 hours at 500 naira an hour to make 600 units. What is the labour cost per unit?
items.s: Labour cost per unit = (1200 x 500)/600 = 1000 naira.

items.q: Budgeted overheads for a year are 1200000 naira and budgeted labour hours are 15000. What is the overhead absorption rate per labour hour?
items.s: Absorption rate = budgeted overheads/budgeted hours = 1200000/15000 = 80 naira per hour.

items.q: Rent of 480000 naira is shared between three departments in the ratio 4:3:2 by floor area. What amount is charged to the first department?
items.s: Share = total x ratio/total ratio = 480000 x 4/9 = 213333.33 naira.

items.q: A department expects to incur 360000 naira of overheads and to run its machines for 1200 hours. What is the machine hour rate?
items.s: Machine hour rate = overheads/machine hours = 360000/1200 = 300 naira per hour.

items.q: A job used 120000 naira of material, 150000 naira of labour and 90000 naira of overheads. The firm quotes a price with a profit of 30 percent on total cost. What is the price?
Work certified on a contract to date is 1500000 naira and the contract provides for retention of 5 percent. What amount is held back?
items.s: Retention = 1500000 x 5/100 = 75000 naira.

items.q: A process finished and transferred 4000 units and left 2000 units in progress which are 25 percent complete. What are the equivalent units of production?
items.s: Equivalent units = completed + closing work in progress x degree of completion = 4000 + 2000 x 25/100 = 4500 units.

items.q: A product sells for 120 naira a unit and has variable costs of 90 naira a unit. Fixed costs are 60000 naira a period and 2000 units are sold. What is the profit?
items.s: Profit = (selling price - variable cost) x units - fixed costs = (120 - 90) x 2000 - 60000 = 0 naira.

items.q: Fixed costs are 180000 naira a period. Each unit sells for 150 naira and has a variable cost of 55 naira. What is the break even point in units?
items.s: Break even units = fixed costs/contribution per unit = 180000/(150 - 55) = 1894.74 units.

items.q: A firm sells 6000 units against a break even volume of 5000 units. Each unit sells for 120 naira. What is the margin of safety in naira?
items.s: Margin of safety = (6000 - 5000) x 120 = 120000 naira.

items.q: Budgeted sales are 9000 units. Opening stock is 500 units and the firm wants 600 units left at the end. How many units must be produced?
items.s: Production = sales + closing stock - opening stock = 9000 + 600 - 500 = 9100 units.

items.q: A cash budget opens with a balance of 80000 naira. Receipts for the month are 360000 naira and payments are 340000 naira. What is the closing balance?
items.s: Closing balance = opening balance + receipts - payments = 80000 + 360000 - 340000 = 100000 naira.

items.q: Production was 2500 units. The standard allowance is 6 kg a unit and 8 kg a unit were actually used. Material is valued at 10 naira a kg. What is the material usage variance?
items.s: Usage variance = (standard quantity - actual quantity) x standard price = (15000 - 20000) x 10 = -50000 naira.

items.q: Workers worked 2000 hours. The standard rate was 300 naira an hour and the actual rate paid was 320 naira an hour. What is the labour rate variance?
items.s: Rate variance = (standard rate - actual rate) x hours = (300 - 320) x 2000 = -40000 naira.

items.q: The reorder level of an item is 3000 units and the reorder quantity is 2000 units. Minimum usage is 200 units a week over a minimum lead time of 2 weeks. What is the maximum stock level?
items.s: Maximum level = reorder level + reorder quantity - (minimum usage x minimum lead time) = 3000 + 2000 - 200 x 2 = 4600 units.

items.q: The value of work certified on an unfinished contract is 900000 naira and the cost incurred to date is 700000 naira. What is the notional profit?
items.s: Notional profit = value certified - cost to date = 900000 - 700000 = 200000 naira.

items.q: A process takes in 5000 units at a total cost of 960000 naira. Normal loss is 10 percent of input and the loss sells for 2 naira a unit. What is the cost per good unit?
items.s: Normal loss = 500 units worth 1000 naira; cost per good unit = (960000 - 1000)/(5000 - 500) = 213.11 naira.

items.q: Fixed costs are 160000 naira and the firm wants a profit of 50000 naira. Each unit contributes 20 naira. How many units must be sold?
items.s: Units = (fixed costs + target profit)/contribution per unit = (160000 + 50000)/20 = 10500 units.

items.q: A firm made 500 units. The standard time allowed is 2 hours a unit and 5 hours a unit were actually worked. The standard rate is 300 naira an hour. What is the labour efficiency variance?
items.s: Efficiency variance = (standard hours - actual hours) x standard rate = (1000 - 2500) x 300 = -450000 naira.

items.q: The correct meaning of indirect expense is
o: an outlay that cannot be traced to one item and must therefore be shared out
an outlay that can be traced wholly to the particular item being made
the sum of direct material, direct labour and direct outlay on a product
the value of the best alternative given up when one choice is preferred to another
items.s: indirect expense: an outlay that cannot be traced to one item and must therefore be shared out. The other options describe prime cost, opportunity cost, direct expense.

items.q: In this course, work in progress refers to
o: goods that have started production but are not complete at the period end
the stage at which items coming from one input become separately identifiable
two or more items of significant value produced together from the same input
the record of quantities and values entering and leaving one stage of production
items.s: work in progress: goods that have started production but are not complete at the period end. The other options describe process account, split off point, joint products.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines marginal costing?
o: spending that stays the same in total whatever the level of output
contribution expressed as a percentage of sales value
the approach that charges only variable spending to products and treats fixed spending as a period item
the excess of actual sales over the break even level
items.s: marginal costing: the approach that charges only variable spending to products and treats fixed spending as a period item. The other options describe margin of safety, fixed cost, profit volume ratio.

items.q: The correct meaning of reorder quantity is
o: the record kept at the store showing quantities received, issued and on hand
the buffer quantity kept against unexpected delays in delivery
the size of the order placed each time the holding falls to the trigger point
the highest holding allowed without risking waste or excess storage charges
items.s: reorder quantity: the size of the order placed each time the holding falls to the trigger point. The other options describe bin card, minimum level, maximum level.

items.q: “the sum of direct material, direct labour and direct outlay on a product” is the definition of
o: prime cost
overhead
opportunity cost
cost unit
items.s: prime cost is the sum of direct material, direct labour and direct outlay on a product.

items.q: The correct meaning of fixed cost is
o: the excess of sales over variable spending, which goes towards fixed spending and profit
spending that stays the same in total whatever the level of output
spending that changes in total in step with the level of output
a future outlay that differs between the options being compared
items.s: fixed cost: spending that stays the same in total whatever the level of output. The other options describe relevant cost, variable cost, contribution.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines absorption rate?
o: a section that supports production without working directly on the product
a single recovery figure applied to the whole factory instead of separate departmental ones
the recovery figure worked out for every unit of running time of a plant item
the amount of indirect spending recovered for each unit of the chosen base
items.s: absorption rate: the amount of indirect spending recovered for each unit of the chosen base. The other options describe blanket rate, machine hour rate, service department.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains prime cost.
o: the total of all spending that cannot be traced to a single item
the sum of direct labour and production overhead needed to turn material into finished goods
an outlay that can be traced wholly to the particular item being made
the sum of direct material, direct labour and direct outlay on a product
items.s: prime cost: the sum of direct material, direct labour and direct outlay on a product. The other options describe conversion cost, overhead, direct expense.

items.q: “the approach that charges only variable spending to products and treats fixed spending as a period item” is the definition of
o: marginal costing
fixed cost
profit volume ratio
relevant cost
items.s: marginal costing is the approach that charges only variable spending to products and treats fixed spending as a period item.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains reorder quantity.
o: the holding at which a fresh order should be placed
the size of the order placed each time the holding falls to the trigger point
the buffer quantity kept against unexpected delays in delivery
the highest holding allowed without risking waste or excess storage charges
items.s: reorder quantity: the size of the order placed each time the holding falls to the trigger point. The other options describe maximum level, minimum level, reorder level.

items.q: In this course, notional profit refers to
o: the excess of approved value over expenditure to date on an unfinished contract
the value of completed construction that the architect of the customer has approved for payment
a term allowing the price to rise if input prices increase during the work
a proportion of the approved value held back until the work is complete
items.s: notional profit: the excess of approved value over expenditure to date on an unfinished contract. The other options describe escalation clause, work certified, retention money.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains abnormal loss.
o: the number of times the average holding is used up during a period
a rate obtained by dividing the total value of goods available by the total quantity
waste above the expected level, which is kept out of the cost of good output
the pricing rule under which the newest consignment is treated as issued first
items.s: abnormal loss: waste above the expected level, which is kept out of the cost of good output. The other options describe weighted average price, lifo, stock turnover.

items.q: In this course, fixed cost refers to
o: spending that stays the same in total whatever the level of output
contribution expressed as a percentage of sales value
the excess of actual sales over the break even level
the approach that charges only variable spending to products and treats fixed spending as a period item
items.s: fixed cost: spending that stays the same in total whatever the level of output. The other options describe marginal costing, profit volume ratio, margin of safety.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains work certified.
o: a term allowing the price to rise if input prices increase during the work
the method used for large long term works carried out at the site of the customer
a proportion of the approved value held back until the work is complete
the value of completed construction that the architect of the customer has approved for payment
items.s: work certified: the value of completed construction that the architect of the customer has approved for payment. The other options describe escalation clause, contract costing, retention money.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains stores ledger.
o: the holding at which a fresh order should be placed
the record kept in the accounts office showing quantity and value of each item
the interval between placing an order and receiving the goods
a situation in which an item is needed for production but none is held
items.s: stores ledger: the record kept in the accounts office showing quantity and value of each item. The other options describe lead time, reorder level, stock out.

items.q: In this course, zero based budget refers to
o: a forecast of the quantities to be made in each period
the practice of comparing actual results with the plan and acting on the differences
a plan restated for the level of activity actually reached
a plan built from nothing so that every item must be justified afresh
items.s: zero based budget: a plan built from nothing so that every item must be justified afresh. The other options describe flexible budget, production budget, budgetary control.

items.q: lead time may be defined as
o: the buffer quantity kept against unexpected delays in delivery
the holding at which a fresh order should be placed
the highest holding allowed without risking waste or excess storage charges
the interval between placing an order and receiving the goods
items.s: lead time: the interval between placing an order and receiving the goods. The other options describe reorder level, maximum level, minimum level.

items.q: The correct meaning of under absorption is
o: the charging of a whole item of spending to the one section that caused it
the situation where less indirect spending is recovered than was actually incurred
the sharing of a common item of spending between sections on an agreed basis
the situation where more indirect spending is recovered than was actually incurred
items.s: under absorption: the situation where less indirect spending is recovered than was actually incurred. The other options describe over absorption, apportionment, allocation.

items.q: variable cost may be defined as
o: the excess of actual sales over the break even level
a future outlay that differs between the options being compared
spending that changes in total in step with the level of output
spending that stays the same in total whatever the level of output
items.s: variable cost: spending that changes in total in step with the level of output. The other options describe fixed cost, margin of safety, relevant cost.

items.q: In this course, margin of safety refers to
o: a future outlay that differs between the options being compared
the excess of sales over variable spending, which goes towards fixed spending and profit
the level of activity at which total revenue equals total spending
the excess of actual sales over the break even level
items.s: margin of safety: the excess of actual sales over the break even level. The other options describe contribution, relevant cost, break even point.

items.q: “the effect on spending of paying more or less than the planned amount for raw stuff bought” is the definition of
o: labour rate variance
material price variance
variance
labour efficiency variance
items.s: material price variance is the effect on spending of paying more or less than the planned amount for raw stuff bought.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “spending that stays the same in total whatever the level of output”
o: relevant cost
fixed cost
margin of safety
break even point
items.s: fixed cost is spending that stays the same in total whatever the level of output.

items.q: apportionment may be defined as
o: the sharing of a common item of spending between sections on an agreed basis
the situation where less indirect spending is recovered than was actually incurred
the situation where more indirect spending is recovered than was actually incurred
the charging of a whole item of spending to the one section that caused it
items.s: apportionment: the sharing of a common item of spending between sections on an agreed basis. The other options describe under absorption, allocation, over absorption.

items.q: The correct meaning of equivalent units is
o: goods that have started production but are not complete at the period end
an item of small value produced incidentally alongside the main output
the expression of partly finished work in terms of fully finished items
two or more items of significant value produced together from the same input
items.s: equivalent units: the expression of partly finished work in terms of fully finished items. The other options describe by product, joint products, work in progress.

items.q: The correct meaning of absorption rate is
o: the situation where less indirect spending is recovered than was actually incurred
the amount of indirect spending recovered for each unit of the chosen base
the situation where more indirect spending is recovered than was actually incurred
a section that supports production without working directly on the product
items.s: absorption rate: the amount of indirect spending recovered for each unit of the chosen base. The other options describe over absorption, under absorption, service department.

items.q: The correct meaning of net pay is
o: the extra above the normal hourly amount paid for hours beyond the standard
the rate at which workers leave and are replaced during a period
the amount a worker actually receives after deductions
a pay system in which the worker receives a fixed amount for each item produced
items.s: net pay: the amount a worker actually receives after deductions. The other options describe labour turnover, piece rate, overtime premium.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains scrap value.
o: a rate obtained by dividing the total value of goods available by the total quantity
the number of times the average holding is used up during a period
the unavoidable waste expected in a process under ordinary working conditions
the amount obtainable by selling waste material
items.s: scrap value: the amount obtainable by selling waste material. The other options describe normal loss, stock turnover, weighted average price.

items.q: “goods that have started production but are not complete at the period end” is the definition of
o: split off point
work in progress
joint products
normal loss account
items.s: work in progress is goods that have started production but are not complete at the period end.

items.q: The correct meaning of piece rate is
o: the total earnings of a worker before any deductions are made
the extra above the normal hourly amount paid for hours beyond the standard
a pay system in which the worker receives a fixed amount for each item produced
work that can be identified with a particular product and charged to it
items.s: piece rate: a pay system in which the worker receives a fixed amount for each item produced. The other options describe direct labour, overtime premium, gross pay.

items.q: “a section of the business for which expenditure is gathered and charged separately” is the definition of
o: cost centre
opportunity cost
sunk cost
indirect expense
items.s: cost centre is a section of the business for which expenditure is gathered and charged separately.

items.q: “an outlay that can be traced wholly to the particular item being made” is the definition of
o: sunk cost
cost unit
direct expense
cost centre
items.s: direct expense is an outlay that can be traced wholly to the particular item being made.

items.q: In this course, process account refers to
o: two or more items of significant value produced together from the same input
an item of small value produced incidentally alongside the main output
the record that carries away the expected waste at its saleable amount
the record of quantities and values entering and leaving one stage of production
items.s: process account: the record of quantities and values entering and leaving one stage of production. The other options describe joint products, by product, normal loss account.

items.q: The correct meaning of notional profit is
o: the excess of approved value over expenditure to date on an unfinished contract
the method used for large long term works carried out at the site of the customer
a proportion of the approved value held back until the work is complete
the method that gathers expenditure separately for each distinct order or batch
items.s: notional profit: the excess of approved value over expenditure to date on an unfinished contract. The other options describe contract costing, retention money, job costing.

items.q: “the effect of paying a different hourly amount from the one planned” is the definition of
o: labour rate variance
material usage variance
favourable variance
variance
items.s: labour rate variance is the effect of paying a different hourly amount from the one planned.

items.q: “the holding at which a fresh order should be placed” is the definition of
o: reorder quantity
bin card
economic order quantity
reorder level
items.s: reorder level is the holding at which a fresh order should be placed.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the size of the order placed each time the holding falls to the trigger point”
o: lead time
bin card
reorder level
reorder quantity
items.s: reorder quantity is the size of the order placed each time the holding falls to the trigger point.

items.q: The correct meaning of labour turnover is
o: work that can be identified with a particular product and charged to it
paid hours during which no production takes place because of breakdown or waiting
the rate at which workers leave and are replaced during a period
the total earnings of a worker before any deductions are made
items.s: labour turnover: the rate at which workers leave and are replaced during a period. The other options describe idle time, direct labour, gross pay.

items.q: “the effect of consuming more or less raw stuff than the quantity allowed for the output” is the definition of
o: labour efficiency variance
material price variance
variance
material usage variance
items.s: material usage variance is the effect of consuming more or less raw stuff than the quantity allowed for the output.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a predetermined figure for what an item should absorb under efficient conditions”
o: variance
material usage variance
standard cost
labour efficiency variance
items.s: standard cost is a predetermined figure for what an item should absorb under efficient conditions.

items.q: equivalent units may be defined as
o: two or more items of significant value produced together from the same input
the expression of partly finished work in terms of fully finished items
the stage at which items coming from one input become separately identifiable
an item of small value produced incidentally alongside the main output
items.s: equivalent units: the expression of partly finished work in terms of fully finished items. The other options describe split off point, by product, joint products.

items.q: “the amount a worker actually receives after deductions” is the definition of
o: net pay
direct labour
idle time
gross pay
items.s: net pay is the amount a worker actually receives after deductions.

items.q: In this course, normal loss account refers to
o: the stage at which items coming from one input become separately identifiable
the record that carries away the expected waste at its saleable amount
two or more items of significant value produced together from the same input
goods that have started production but are not complete at the period end
items.s: normal loss account: the record that carries away the expected waste at its saleable amount. The other options describe work in progress, split off point, joint products.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains budget.
o: a forecast of money coming in and going out during the period
a written plan of expected income and spending for a stated future period
the practice of comparing actual results with the plan and acting on the differences
a plan built from nothing so that every item must be justified afresh
items.s: budget: a written plan of expected income and spending for a stated future period. The other options describe zero based budget, cash budget, budgetary control.

items.q: The correct meaning of favourable variance is
o: a difference that raises profit compared with the plan
the difference between a planned figure and the figure actually recorded
the effect on spending of paying more or less than the planned amount for raw stuff bought
a predetermined figure for what an item should absorb under efficient conditions
items.s: favourable variance: a difference that raises profit compared with the plan. The other options describe material price variance, variance, standard cost.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains cash budget.
o: a forecast of money coming in and going out during the period
a written plan of expected income and spending for a stated future period
a plan built from nothing so that every item must be justified afresh
the practice of comparing actual results with the plan and acting on the differences
items.s: cash budget: a forecast of money coming in and going out during the period. The other options describe budget, budgetary control, zero based budget.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines work certified?
o: the method used for large long term works carried out at the site of the customer
the method that gathers expenditure separately for each distinct order or batch
a proportion of the approved value held back until the work is complete
the value of completed construction that the architect of the customer has approved for payment
items.s: work certified: the value of completed construction that the architect of the customer has approved for payment. The other options describe retention money, job costing, contract costing.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains budgetary control.
o: the practice of comparing actual results with the plan and acting on the differences
a written plan of expected income and spending for a stated future period
a plan restated for the level of activity actually reached
a forecast of the quantities to be made in each period
items.s: budgetary control: the practice of comparing actual results with the plan and acting on the differences. The other options describe flexible budget, production budget, budget.

items.q: “the size of the order placed each time the holding falls to the trigger point” is the definition of
o: stores ledger
maximum level
reorder quantity
minimum level
items.s: reorder quantity is the size of the order placed each time the holding falls to the trigger point.

items.q: “the difference between a planned figure and the figure actually recorded” is the definition of
o: standard cost
material price variance
favourable variance
variance
items.s: variance is the difference between a planned figure and the figure actually recorded.

items.q: The correct meaning of production budget is
o: a plan restated for the level of activity actually reached
a plan built from nothing so that every item must be justified afresh
a forecast of the quantities to be made in each period
a forecast of money coming in and going out during the period
items.s: production budget: a forecast of the quantities to be made in each period. The other options describe zero based budget, flexible budget, cash budget.

items.q: The correct meaning of minimum level is
o: the batch size at which the cost of placing orders and the cost of keeping stock together reach their lowest
the buffer quantity kept against unexpected delays in delivery
a situation in which an item is needed for production but none is held
the record kept in the accounts office showing quantity and value of each item
items.s: minimum level: the buffer quantity kept against unexpected delays in delivery. The other options describe stores ledger, stock out, economic order quantity.

items.q: In this course, scrap value refers to
o: the practice of charging each issue with the exact amount paid for that consignment
the pricing rule under which the newest consignment is treated as issued first
the amount obtainable by selling waste material
a rate obtained by dividing the total value of goods available by the total quantity
items.s: scrap value: the amount obtainable by selling waste material. The other options describe lifo, specific price, weighted average price.

items.q: In this course, marginal costing refers to
o: spending that changes in total in step with the level of output
a future outlay that differs between the options being compared
the level of activity at which total revenue equals total spending
the approach that charges only variable spending to products and treats fixed spending as a period item
items.s: marginal costing: the approach that charges only variable spending to products and treats fixed spending as a period item. The other options describe break even point, relevant cost, variable cost.

items.q: The correct meaning of bin card is
o: the batch size at which the cost of placing orders and the cost of keeping stock together reach their lowest
the size of the order placed each time the holding falls to the trigger point
the highest holding allowed without risking waste or excess storage charges
the record kept at the store showing quantities received, issued and on hand
items.s: bin card: the record kept at the store showing quantities received, issued and on hand. The other options describe reorder quantity, economic order quantity, maximum level.

items.q: The correct meaning of overhead is
o: the total of all spending that cannot be traced to a single item
an outlay that can be traced wholly to the particular item being made
the sum of direct material, direct labour and direct outlay on a product
an outlay that cannot be traced to one item and must therefore be shared out
items.s: overhead: the total of all spending that cannot be traced to a single item. The other options describe indirect expense, direct expense, prime cost.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains absorption.
o: a single recovery figure applied to the whole factory instead of separate departmental ones
the recovery of indirect spending into the figure carried by each product using a chosen rate
the situation where less indirect spending is recovered than was actually incurred
the amount of indirect spending recovered for each unit of the chosen base
items.s: absorption: the recovery of indirect spending into the figure carried by each product using a chosen rate. The other options describe blanket rate, absorption rate, under absorption.

items.q: “the situation where less indirect spending is recovered than was actually incurred” is the definition of
o: allocation
service department
under absorption
machine hour rate
items.s: under absorption is the situation where less indirect spending is recovered than was actually incurred.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the level of activity at which total revenue equals total spending”
o: margin of safety
break even point
fixed cost
variable cost
items.s: break even point is the level of activity at which total revenue equals total spending.

items.q: overtime premium may be defined as
o: the extra above the normal hourly amount paid for hours beyond the standard
paid hours during which no production takes place because of breakdown or waiting
a pay system in which the worker receives a fixed amount for each hour worked
the rate at which workers leave and are replaced during a period
items.s: overtime premium: the extra above the normal hourly amount paid for hours beyond the standard. The other options describe labour turnover, time rate, idle time.

items.q: In this course, material price variance refers to
o: the effect of working faster or slower than the hours allowed
the effect of consuming more or less raw stuff than the quantity allowed for the output
the effect on spending of paying more or less than the planned amount for raw stuff bought
a predetermined figure for what an item should absorb under efficient conditions
items.s: material price variance: the effect on spending of paying more or less than the planned amount for raw stuff bought. The other options describe material usage variance, standard cost, labour efficiency variance.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines joint products?
o: the expression of partly finished work in terms of fully finished items
the record of quantities and values entering and leaving one stage of production
two or more items of significant value produced together from the same input
the record that carries away the expected waste at its saleable amount
items.s: joint products: two or more items of significant value produced together from the same input. The other options describe normal loss account, equivalent units, process account.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the total earnings of a worker before any deductions are made”
o: time rate
direct labour
piece rate
gross pay
items.s: gross pay is the total earnings of a worker before any deductions are made.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines split off point?
o: the record of quantities and values entering and leaving one stage of production
the expression of partly finished work in terms of fully finished items
the stage at which items coming from one input become separately identifiable
goods that have started production but are not complete at the period end
items.s: split off point: the stage at which items coming from one input become separately identifiable. The other options describe process account, equivalent units, work in progress.

items.q: “contribution expressed as a percentage of sales value” is the definition of
o: break even point
fixed cost
profit volume ratio
contribution
items.s: profit volume ratio is contribution expressed as a percentage of sales value.

items.q: The correct meaning of absorption is
o: the recovery of indirect spending into the figure carried by each product using a chosen rate
the sharing of a common item of spending between sections on an agreed basis
the recovery figure worked out for every unit of running time of a plant item
the charging of a whole item of spending to the one section that caused it
items.s: absorption: the recovery of indirect spending into the figure carried by each product using a chosen rate. The other options describe allocation, apportionment, machine hour rate.
